observations.statement: Every failed or non-executed attempt is classified before policy as one canonical failure class or blocked-episode cause; distinct outcome families must remain distinct, and generic retry before classification is prohibited.

The outcome matrix fixes retry counts and backoff for provider-transient, rate-limited, structured-output, auth-expiry, storage-I/O, quota, graph-integrity, permission, approval, FileSafe, external-side-effect, and replan outcomes; unknown classifiers fail closed as validation-blocked.

The doom-loop match key is tool name, canonical serialized argument hash, and error message at the same nesting level; the later alignment names kill.identical_failure as terminal and stop.identical_failure as a compatibility alias.

MCP listTools discovery retries three times with one-second backoff and then uses the last-known stale inventory until a five-minute refresh succeeds; discovery failure alone cannot permanently kill the executor, provider session, or run.

Regex-index builds expose explicit lifecycle states, one build slot per project, pending-plan supersession, cancellation-token checks between file iterations, partial-generation cleanup, FIFO admission under shared-pool saturation, and prevention of concurrent generation-directory writes.

All listed stream adapters use one coalescer; only a final assistant turn with its matching receipt may enter durable assistant history, terminal inactivity times out after 5000 ms as provider-transient, and frame or byte overflow fails structurally as validation-blocked without silent dropping.

Entrypoints create a once-owned shutdown root before subprocess launch; provider processes have a five-second signal grace window, MCP and LSP processes have three seconds, SIGHUP reloads configuration, and managed subprocesses use isolated process groups.

Every mutation-capable node attempt must create or attach a runtime safe point containing run, node, attempt, execution-root, baseline, generation, and applicable worktree identity; safe points are recovery anchors rather than user restore or thread-rewind points.

Automatic remediation remains child lineage of the failed attempt, preserves finding identifiers, delays parent retry until remediation and retry policy permit it, and creates a canonical graph node only when replan changes scope.

Only invalid pre-canonical draft decomposition may flatten deterministically with warning evidence; invalid canonical graphs fail as graph-integrity, and required rich artifacts, tools, browser, or web surfaces cannot silently degrade to text-only output.

Scheduler execution is a deterministic capacity-aware pass using the tuple scheduler_lane, manual_priority, transitive_unblock_count, ready_since_utc, and node_id; readiness also checks lifecycle, blockers, backoff, runtime projections, generation, worktree conflicts, and lane or pool capacity.

Each scheduler wake synchronously reevaluates affected dependents, builds a global ready set, emits queue analysis keyed by scheduler_pass_id, selects up to available slots in score order, and admits newly unblocked direct dependents before that dispatch cycle completes.

Rich editor and workbench callers share execution_unit_context with terminal, browser, document, and artifact callers; blocked and degraded conditions must preserve attempt identity, safe points, worktree binding, review visibility, and autonomy defaults, while GUI setup exposes sign-in or API-key choices.

Runtime overlays remain separate from graph lifecycle, blocked_sequence persists across repeated updates and startup recovery, retries and restored reruns mint new immutable attempt records, and execution_unit_context is the authoritative shared runtime scope instead of retired tier-era context.

A run stays active while any node is runnable, becomes deferred rather than terminal when only blocked, backoff, or prerequisite-waiting work remains, and wakes for prerequisite, restore, remediation, authentication, or capacity changes.

Attempt accounting requires attempt_count to equal the four cause-specific attempt counters plus the initial attempt; sub-counters increment at attempt start and independent policy counters cannot be derived by subtraction.

candidate_findings.summary: Several required classifier codes lack a closed executor policy entry.
candidate_findings.obligation: Search and SSH handoffs must use named network, trust, permission, and path codes, and every non-success outcome must be classified before policy.
candidate_findings.gap: The matrix does not assign classifier families, retry behavior, recovery actions, or terminal behavior to network_blocked_by_policy, host_unreachable, host_untrusted, path_not_found, auth_required, validation blockers, worktree conflicts, or dirty worktrees, leaving materially different executor behavior possible.

candidate_findings.summary: The required doom-loop terminal event is internally inconsistent.
candidate_findings.obligation: A repeated identical failure must immediately terminate the run and emit the canonical terminal outcome.
candidate_findings.gap: One normative rule requires stop.identical_failure, while the later alignment declares kill.identical_failure terminal and stop.identical_failure only an older alias; it does not say whether implementations emit one, both, or select by compatibility version.

candidate_findings.summary: Some retry timing remains implementation-defined.
candidate_findings.obligation: Rate-limited and storage-I/O outcomes have bounded automatic retries with specified backoff behavior.
candidate_findings.gap: Storage-I/O uses the undefined duration brief delay, and rate limiting does not define Retry-After parsing, invalid-value handling, or a maximum accepted delay, so retry timing is not exact.

candidate_findings.summary: The degraded listTools path has no cold-start behavior.
candidate_findings.obligation: After three one-second retries, listTools discovery must use the last-known stale tool list until periodic refresh succeeds.
candidate_findings.gap: The contract does not define the result when no last-known list exists, whether three means total attempts or retries after an initial attempt, or which state and capabilities are exposed during that interval.

candidate_findings.summary: Regex-index cancellation lacks a terminal FSM transition.
candidate_findings.obligation: Superseded builds cancel through a token, clean partial generation directories, and failures or cancellation use classified paths.
candidate_findings.gap: The stated FSM only names ready and error destinations; it does not specify the index state, pending-plan disposition, or observable receipt after cancellation or supersession cleanup.

candidate_findings.summary: Stream settlement and timeout edge behavior is underspecified.
candidate_findings.obligation: Only final_assistant_turn plus its matching receipt may become durable history; missing terminal events time out after 5000 ms, and bounded overflow cannot silently drop frames.
candidate_findings.gap: The contract does not define the timeout clock start or reset condition, how the matching receipt is identified, the outcome when a final turn arrives without its receipt, or how queued frames are drained or discarded after timeout or overflow.

candidate_findings.summary: Subprocess behavior after grace-window expiry is undefined.
candidate_findings.obligation: Managed provider, MCP, and LSP subprocesses receive signals with fixed grace windows in isolated process groups.
candidate_findings.gap: The contract does not specify which of SIGTERM or SIGINT is sent in each shutdown path, whether and when force-kill follows, how descendants are reaped, or what run outcome is recorded when a process survives its grace window.

candidate_findings.summary: Safe-point worktree branch field names conflict.
candidate_findings.obligation: A worktree safe-point payload must carry the checked-out branch and the required worktree-bound attempt properties.
candidate_findings.gap: The payload table names worktree_branch, while the required-property list names branch_name; no aliasing or canonical serialization rule resolves which field producers and consumers must use.

candidate_findings.summary: Safe-point attachment and attempt reuse boundaries are not exact.
candidate_findings.obligation: Each mutation-capable attempt creates or attaches a safe point containing attempt_id, while retries, prerequisite resumes, and safe-point-restored reruns create new attempt IDs.
candidate_findings.gap: The contract permits creating or attaching a safe point and creating or reusing an attempt ID but does not define when attachment or reuse is legal, whether a safe point is unique per attempt, or how an attached safe point is rebound when a restored rerun must mint a new attempt.

candidate_findings.summary: Remediation generation uses two incompatible field names.
candidate_findings.obligation: Automatic remediation must record its generation as part of child lineage.
candidate_findings.gap: The first lineage rule requires generation, while the later alignment requires remediation_generation; the capsule supplies no canonical field or compatibility mapping.

candidate_findings.summary: Deterministic draft flattening lacks an ordering contract.
candidate_findings.obligation: Invalid pre-lock draft decomposition may degrade only to deterministic flat sequencing with warning evidence.
candidate_findings.gap: No ordering key, tie-break rule, warning event name, required warning fields, or persistence location is defined, so builders can produce different supposedly deterministic sequences and evidence.

candidate_findings.summary: Queue-analysis and capacity allocation are not implementation-complete.
candidate_findings.obligation: Queue analysis must explain both winners and ready-but-unselected nodes before deterministic capacity-aware dispatch, keyed by scheduler_pass_id.
candidate_findings.gap: No queue-analysis record schema, candidate reason codes, score snapshot requirements, available_slots computation, lane or pool reservation rule, or behavior when global and lane capacity disagree is specified.

candidate_findings.summary: Rich-surface recovery conditions have no closed event mapping.
candidate_findings.obligation: Authentication friction, reconnect loss, disabled-feature fallbacks, indexing cost, performance pressure, and workbench clutter must surface as explicit blocked, degraded, backoff, or recovery events; browser handoff uses pause and resume, and manual boundaries become attention_required.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule does not map each condition to one state or event, define the attention_required classifier family and resume prerequisites, or specify automation-session identity and pause/resume transition receipts.

candidate_findings.summary: Blocked UI action authorization and projection fields are incomplete.
candidate_findings.obligation: Checkpoint, approve or deny, retry, and resolution actions are keyed by blocked_sequence and allowed_action_ids, and blocked episodes must have one canonical cause.
candidate_findings.gap: No action-ID catalog, request or result schema, idempotency rule, authorization failure behavior, or state transition is given; additionally, node-blocked is said to own failure_class but no location is specified for the blocked_reason_code required by blocked episodes.

candidate_findings.summary: Automatic PM Outdated reprojection has no enforceable safety predicate.
candidate_findings.obligation: At launch, a PM Outdated projection should auto-reproject before run launch when safe.
candidate_findings.gap: The use of should and the undefined when-safe predicate leave builders discretion over whether launch blocks, proceeds with stale state, prompts the user, or records a reprojection failure.

candidate_findings.summary: Graph-lock failure does not define the fate of running attempts.
candidate_findings.obligation: After run.graph_canonical_locked, invalid graph structure is graph_integrity, new dispatches stop, and no degraded canonical execution is allowed.
candidate_findings.gap: The contract does not state whether already-running attempts drain, cancel, roll back, or become blocked, nor which event and final run state record the lock violation.

candidate_findings.summary: Blocked-episode carry-through lists required data without defining its durable contract.
candidate_findings.obligation: Restart recovery must preserve blocked_sequence, approval scope, execution role, requested account, operational identity, switch and pressure ownership, and durable approver identity.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule gives no field names or types for most carry-through data, no approval or rejection event shape, and no rule for creating a new sequence after a prior episode resolves.

candidate_findings.summary: Provider and model precedence is requested but not defined.
candidate_findings.obligation: One owner section must establish precedence across run, seam, package, node, overseer, and delegated-subagent scopes and tie resolution to parallel worktree ownership; auto selection must be explainable by actor-type mapping.
candidate_findings.gap: No precedence order, conflict-resolution algorithm, inheritance rule, actor-to-account/model/persona mapping, or worktree reassignment transition is present, so requested and effective provider identity can vary by implementation.

candidate_findings.summary: The attempt-count invariant omits a named rerun cause.
candidate_findings.obligation: Every retry, prerequisite resume, and safe-point-restored rerun creates a new attempt, while attempt_count must equal four cause counters plus the initial attempt.
candidate_findings.gap: The formula has no safe-point_restore_count, and no rule assigns a safe-point-restored rerun to automatic, prerequisite, manual, or remediation counters; it also does not resolve attempts with more than one triggering cause, risking an unsatisfiable or inconsistently applied invariant.

candidate_findings.summary: Deferred-run projection and verification completion remain underspecified.
candidate_findings.obligation: A run with only blocked, backoff, or prerequisite-waiting work is deferred and wakes on named recovery causes; agent-session verification passes only after non-recurrence and the adapter's expected terminal state.
candidate_findings.gap: No deferred state or event name, persistence transition, wake deduplication rule, or per-adapter expected terminal-state table is supplied.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Provider-transient backoff is exact: three retries at 1s, 2s, and 4s, with base 1s, factor 2x, and cap 4s.
Verifier failure and reviewer findings are explicitly separate non-auto-retry classes, and malformed structured output has exactly two immediate retries.
Unknown classifier values explicitly fail closed as blocked_reason_code validation_blocked until governance extends the owning enum.
Backpressure limits are exact at 1024 pending frames or 16777216 pending bytes, whichever is reached first, with no silent frame drop.
Safe points explicitly require run_id, node_id, attempt_id, execution root, pre-attempt baseline references, and active replan_generation before mutation-capable execution.
The scheduler score order and all five term definitions are explicit, including manual_priority range and default, continuously-ready timestamp reset, and node_id as final tiebreak only.
Direct blocked-to-runnable propagation is explicitly synchronous in the same wake and enters the same ready set without an extra scheduler pass.
Waiting approval, safe-point state, and remediation state explicitly remain runtime overlays rather than new graph lifecycle values.
Repeated blocked updates and startup recovery explicitly retain an existing blocked_sequence rather than reminting it.
Every retry, prerequisite resume, and safe-point-restored rerun explicitly gets a new attempt_id, and prior attempts remain immutable.
Retired tier-era context may only be derived for legacy selection or decomposition and may not be persisted, exchanged, or rehydrated as live runtime scope.
GUI truth explicitly includes a sticky, dismissible, reviewable draft Plan panel for pre-execution auto-use and user-visible Sign in with ChatGPT and Use API Key setup choices.

unknowns.reason: The excerpt assigns ownership to Contracts_V0 and other contracts while showing only a partial matrix and several additional codes.

unknowns.reason: The capsule makes that object authoritative and references Primitive:ExecutionContext but does not enumerate its fields.

unknowns.reason: Persisted executor events are required to consume an external envelope and schema whose field set is not reproduced in this capsule.

unknowns.statement: Provider-specific stream resume constants and circuit-breaker thresholds are unknown.
unknowns.reason: The excerpt requires at most three reconnects and open, half-open, close, or reopen transitions but delegates provider-specific constants without stating them.

unknowns.statement: The exact allowed_action_ids vocabulary and blocked action result contracts are unknown.
unknowns.reason: The capsule requires those identifiers for UI runtime actions but does not enumerate them or their payloads.

unknowns.statement: The canonical provider and model precedence order is unknown.
unknowns.reason: The acceptance carry-through says an owner section must define precedence across scopes, but no such ordering appears in the capsule.
